newsitem.title: USA: Lawyer for British nanny appeals for bail.
newsitem.headline: Lawyer for British nanny appeals for bail.

text.p: The lawyer for a British nanny accused of first-degree murder in the death of a nine-month old boy in her care appealed on Wednesday to the highest court in Massachusetts to have the 19-year-old released on bail.
Louise Woodward, a Chester, England, au pair who came to the United States in June 1996, has been in the state's women's prison facility since her arrest in early February.

"This is a woman who is dependable, reliable, has all the characteristics of a what we would consider a good bail risk," Woodward's attorney Harvey Silverglate told the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court, citing letters of support for Woodward from her parish vicar, school headmistress, family doctor and others in his appeal.
Prosecutor Lynn Rooney told Justice Charles Fried that most of the letters in support of Woodward were written by people who did not know her personally.

She said Woodward had no ties to Massachusetts and any bail offered for her would not be her own money. Furthermore, Woodward did not personally know the people who have submitted letters on her behalf and felt no obligation to them, Rooney added.
"This particular defendant poses a significant risk of flight," Rooney concluded.

Woodward was jailed in the death of Matthew Eappen, who was left in her charge at the Eappen family home in Newton, Massachusetts. The boy was severely shaken for at least 60 seconds before his head was hit against a hard surface, causing a skull fracture, prosecutors said.
Justice Fried reserved judgment on the question of bail. A trial is scheduled to begin on July 14.
